raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

With UVA weight offloading (`--offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-gb N --cpu-offload-params experts`), the fused-MoE kernel reads offloaded experts from host memory in place, once per M-tile (64 tokens with the default config here) of the tokens routed to each expert, so in prefill every offloaded expert crosses PCIe several times per step. This adds an opt-in `--cpu-offload-stage-min-tokens` (default 0 = off; `auto` = every step that runs without CUDA graphs): such steps copy each layer's offloaded `w1`/`w2` into a reusable device buffer right before the expert kernel, which reads the copy. Decode and every graph-captured step keep today's zero-copy reads.

## Claims

vLLM 0.31.0 with this patch against stock 0.31.0; Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8, one RTX 4090 (PCIe 4.0 x16), 16 GiB of experts offloaded.

- **End to end** (16 multi-turn sessions, 16–19k-token prompts, 4 turns, 2 in flight; 3 interleaved runs per arm, spread < 0.1%): wall time **1.785× shorter at 2048-token chunks, 2.687× at 8192**; new-session TTFT p50 17.52 → 8.51 s and 21.89 → 4.93 s.
- **Decode unchanged** (ShareGPT at 1 and 4 in flight within 0.05 tok/s). **Exact:** staging off vs `auto` in one build gives byte-identical greedy output on 18/18 requests; GSM8K 0.896 vs 0.900 (±0.019) against stock.
- **Cost:** one buffer per offloaded expert-weight shape (576 MiB here), allocated in the profiling run so the KV cache is sized with it: −6,144 KV tokens at 8192-token chunks (exactly the buffers), −6,752 at 2048 (~57 MiB more, not traced).
- **235B-A22B FP8, TP8** (16 GiB experts/GPU, one run per arm): 1.52× on 4 sessions × 2 turns at 1 in flight, 1.39× on a following 16-request run at 2 in flight; decode unchanged. Not checked for identical output: this setup is not reproducible run to run even without the patch.

## Validation

```
pytest tests/model_executor/offloader/                        # RTX 4090: 15 passed
pytest tests/basic_correctness/cpu_offload/test_cpu_offload.py   # RTX 4090: 11 passed (3 new + the existing offload tests)
```
Run on the nightly wheel of this PR's base commit with the patched files applied (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14).

- Unit tests: `auto`/0/N resolution (in `VllmConfig`, excluded from `compute_hash`); pass-through below the threshold, for non-offloaded weights and when off; an identical copy that keeps strides, one buffer reused across layers, separate buffers per slot; no staging or allocation inside a CUDA graph capture; and through `FusedMoEKernel.apply` (Triton experts): at the threshold the experts receive the staging buffers (checked by `data_ptr`) and match the same weights in VRAM, one token below they receive the UVA views.
- End to end: `TitanML/tiny-mixtral` (eager, every step staged; CUDA graphs, prefill staged) and `Adamji/tiny-qwen3-moe-fp8-per-block` (CUDA graphs), threshold off vs on: identical greedy output.
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`: no sync error. Pre-commit hooks pass.

| setup (30B unless noted) | metric | base | PR (`auto`) | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| agent workload, chunk 2048 | wall s; new-session TTFT p50 | 1154.9 (1154.7–1155.0); 17.52 s | 646.9 (646.8–646.9); 8.51 s | 1.785×; 2.06× |
| same, chunk 8192 | wall s; new-session TTFT p50 | 1030.7 (1030.5–1030.9); 21.89 s | 383.5 (383.4–383.8); 4.93 s | 2.687×; 4.44× |
| ShareGPT 256 out, 1 / 4 in flight | output tok/s | 20.83 / 22.87 | 20.88 / 22.92 | none |
| KV cache, chunk 2048 / 8192 | tokens | 75,504 / 68,480 | 68,752 / 62,336 | −6,752 / −6,144 |
| GSM8K (lm-eval, 250, greedy) | exact match flexible / strict | 0.900 / 0.880 | 0.896 / 0.876 | within ±0.02 |
| 235B TP8, `--numa-bind`, chunk 2048, 1 run | 4 sessions × 2 turns at 1 in flight, wall s; ShareGPT c4 tok/s | 111.0; 18.77 | 72.8; 18.90 | 1.52×; none |

<details>
<summary>Server command and kernel microbenchmark</summary>

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-gb 16 --cpu-offload-params experts \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --cpu-offload-stage-min-tokens auto
```

One step through all 48 MoE layers (checkpoint FP8 block shapes, random weights, routing from recorded chat traffic): the MoE part is 2.4× faster at 2048 tokens, 6.9× at 8192, 11.3× at 16384. UVA reads 2.32× / 7.75× / 15.05× the offloaded bytes per step; the copy reads them once at 26.3 GB/s. Copying loses below 256–512 tokens (0.91× at 256) and wins from 512 (1.09×), which is what `auto`'s floor of 512 is based on.

Clients: the agent rows replay 16 long ShareGPT conversations as sessions (turn 0 sends the first ≥16k tokens of the conversation, each later turn appends the dataset's next exchange, so prompts are 16–19k tokens and each extends the previous one; 4 turns, 64 output tokens per turn, 2 sessions in flight) with [`agent_sessions.py` + `agent_load.py`](https://gist.github.com/mushroomcarbon/a84affdf83e8e3be9269e3985030a1f8) (exact commands in their headers); the decode rows are `vllm bench serve --dataset-name sharegpt --sharegpt-output-len 256 --ignore-eos --max-concurrency 1|4`; GSM8K is `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --limit 250` (greedy).
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `fused_moe_kernel` gives each program one M-tile of one expert and streams that expert's weights, so every tile re-reads the expert. In VRAM that is cheap; over UVA each re-read crosses PCIe (0.97–0.98 host reads per tile). A tuned `BLOCK_SIZE_M` 128 config helps UVA 1.4–1.9× but copying in is still 1.1–6× faster, and it slows the all-in-VRAM case 8–12% at ≥ 2048 tokens.

**Design.** `BaseOffloader.maybe_stage(weight, num_tokens, slot)` returns the weight unchanged except in `UVAOffloader`, whose `UVAExpertStager` copies a weight carrying the UVA marker when the step meets the threshold and the stream is not capturing. `FusedMoEKernelModularImpl.apply` calls it for `w1`/`w2` after `_prepare`, unless the experts set `reads_weight_args = False` (FlashInfer MoE-EP and b12x run on weights prepared at load time). It is a copy, not a cache: no routing inspection (no device-to-host sync), no eviction, any layout the kernel reads, nothing to invalidate after EPLB or weight updates. One buffer per (slot, shape, stride, dtype, device) is shared by all layers; copy and kernel run on the same stream, so layer l+1's copy waits for layer l's kernel (also under DBO, whose micro-batches share the stream). `auto` resolves in `VllmConfig.__post_init__` to `max(max_cudagraph_capture_size + 1, 512)`; an explicit N at or below the capture size warns, since captured steps never stage. The threshold is left out of `compute_hash` (it acts inside the opaque `moe_forward` op). Like the other offload options, the flag is documented through the CLI help; there is no offload docs page to extend.

**Why opt-in.** It shrinks the KV cache of every `--cpu-offload-gb` user by the buffers (several GiB for large BF16 MoE layers), and it is unmeasured on NVLink-C2C systems and APUs, where reading in place may already be fast enough.

**Limitations.** CUDA only: ROCm AITER kernels read a per-tensor attribute (`is_shuffled`) that the buffer does not carry, and a backend keyed on the weight's `data_ptr` would see one address for every layer (none in the modular path is); such backends must opt out via `reads_weight_args`. Measured with Triton experts and FP8 block weights only; FlashInfer, DeepGEMM and CUTLASS experts untested. Only the modular fused-MoE path; monolithic kernels read in place as before. Under DBO each micro-batch copies the layer. With all2all EP the threshold counts tokens before dispatch. The buffers are not in the sleep-mode pool, and come on top of `--kv-cache-memory-bytes`. Copy and compute are sequential: double-buffering would save 4% at 2048-token steps and 12–19% at 8k–16k (microbenchmark), for a second buffer; left as a follow-up.

**Not a duplicate.** #37190 (open) is an opt-in GPU expert *cache*: it inspects routing each forward (`topk_ids.unique().tolist()`, a sync per layer), copies missing experts one by one, evicts with LFRU, and runs the MoE layer outside CUDA graphs (it caps `cudagraph_mode` at PIECEWISE). RFC #38256 asks to load each distinct expert once in batched prefill; this is the narrow form of that for the existing UVA path. Residency work (#54610, #56177, #57794, #57943) decides which experts live in VRAM; this composes with it, since only weights carrying the UVA marker are staged. #51710 extends the *prefetch* backend, which copies every step including decode. #54972 edits a different `UVAOffloader` method. Searched 2026-10-09 and rechecked 2026-10-16: none stages UVA experts for large steps.

**AI assistance.** Claude Opus 5.5 assisted with the code, tests, benchmarks and this description; the tests and benchmarks above were run on my hardware. I reviewed every changed line and the results, and can answer for it; the commit carries an `Assisted-by:` trailer.

@@ -141,3 +142,56 @@ def test_tower_weight_offloading(vllm_runner, monkeypatch, disable_uva):
     finally:
         set_offloader(original_offloader)

+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="staging is CUDA only")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("model", "eager", "threshold"),
+    # Eager: every step stages. Graphs up to 8 tokens: only the prefill
+    # (longer than 8 tokens) stages, decode replays graphs that read in place.
+    [
+        ("TitanML/tiny-mixtral", True, 1),
+        ("TitanML/tiny-mixtral", False, 9),
+        ("Adamji/tiny-qwen3-moe-fp8-per-block", False, 9),
+    ],
+)
+def test_uva_expert_staging(vllm_runner, monkeypatch, model, eager, threshold):
+    """Staging UVA-offloaded experts gives the same greedy output as reading
+    them in place (threshold 0)."""
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING", "0")
+    envs.disable_envs_cache()
+    original_offloader = get_offloader()
+    prompts = [
+        "The capital of France is a city that many people like to visit because",
+        "Here is a short story about a robot who learned to paint the sea:",
+    ]
+    outputs = {}
+
+    try:
+        for min_tokens in (0, threshold):
+            with vllm_runner(
+                model,
+                enforce_eager=eager,
+                compilation_config=(
+                    None if eager else {"cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4, 8]}
+                ),
+                moe_backend="triton",
+                gpu_memory_utilization=0.3,
+                max_model_len=256,
+                max_num_seqs=2,
+                cpu_offload_gb=1,
+                cpu_offload_params={"experts"},
+                cpu_offload_stage_min_tokens=min_tokens,
+            ) as vllm_model:
+                offloader = get_offloader()
+                assert isinstance(offloader, UVAOffloader)
+                assert offloader.cpu_offload_bytes > 0
+                assert offloader.expert_stager.min_tokens == min_tokens
+                outputs[min_tokens] = vllm_model.generate_greedy(prompts, 16)
+                # Buffers exist only if a step was staged.
+                assert bool(offloader.expert_stager._buffers) == (min_tokens > 0)
+    finally:
+        set_offloader(original_offloader)
+        envs.disable_envs_cache()
+
+    assert outputs[0] == outputs[threshold]

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Staging of UVA-offloaded fused-MoE expert weights for large steps."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn as nn
+
+from vllm.config import OffloadConfig, UVAOffloadConfig, VllmConfig
+from vllm.model_executor.offloader.uva import UVAExpertStager, UVAOffloader
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.platform_utils import is_uva_available
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skip_global_cleanup
+
+
+def _offloaded(t: torch.Tensor) -> nn.Parameter:
+    """A parameter carrying the UVA offloader's marker."""
+    p = nn.Parameter(t, requires_grad=False)
+    p._vllm_is_uva_offloaded = True
+    return p
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def cpu_stream(monkeypatch):
+    """The copy path asks the current stream whether it is capturing; CPU-only
+    runs have no device stream to ask. Capture itself is tested on CUDA."""
+    stream = SimpleNamespace(is_capturing=lambda: False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.accelerator, "current_stream", lambda: stream)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("value", "max_capture_size", "expected"),
+    [
+        ("AUTO", 512, 513),  # every step that runs without CUDA graphs
+        ("auto", 0, 512),  # no CUDA graphs: never below 512
+        (0, 512, 0),  # disabled (the default)
+        (2048, 512, 2048),
+    ],
+)
+def test_resolve_stage_min_tokens(value, max_capture_size, expected):
+    config = UVAOffloadConfig(cpu_offload_stage_min_tokens=value)
+    assert config.resolve_stage_min_tokens(max_capture_size) == expected
+
+
+def test_vllm_config_resolves_auto_and_hash_ignores_it():

+class UVAExpertStager:
+    """Copies UVA-offloaded expert weights into a device buffer for steps of
+    at least `min_tokens` tokens (0 disables), see
+    `UVAOffloadConfig.cpu_offload_stage_min_tokens`.
+
+    One buffer per (slot, shape, stride, dtype, device) is shared by all
+    layers. The copy and the kernel reading the buffer are issued on the same
+    stream, so layer l+1's copy waits for layer l's kernel. Under DBO both
+    micro-batches use one compute stream, so the caller must not yield between
+    staging and the experts kernel.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, min_tokens: int):
+        self.min_tokens = min_tokens
+        self._buffers: dict[tuple, torch.Tensor] = {}
+
+    def maybe_stage(
+        self, weight: torch.Tensor, num_tokens: int, slot: str
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if (
+            self.min_tokens == 0
+            or num_tokens < self.min_tokens
+            or not getattr(weight, "_vllm_is_uva_offloaded", False)
+            # A captured copy would replay at every size the graph serves.
+            or torch.accelerator.current_stream().is_capturing()
+        ):
+            return weight
+        key = (slot, tuple(weight.shape), weight.stride(), weight.dtype, weight.device)
+        buf = self._buffers.get(key)

+            # for it.
+            buf = torch.empty_strided(

+                format_gib(buf.numel() * buf.element_size()),
+                slot,
+                tuple(weight.shape),
+                weight.dtype,
+            )
+        buf.copy_(weight, non_blocking=True)
+        return buf
